title: Mini Crochet Sunflower
name: Mini Sunflower
subtitle: No-Sew Crochet Pattern
tagline: Free crochet pattern | Beginner friendly | No sew | Printable
seoTitle: Easy Crochet Sunflower Pattern for Beginners (Free, No Sew)
description: Free, easy mini crochet sunflower pattern for beginners. Two brown centres join with yellow petals, so there is no sewing. Printable, with a round chart.
lead: A small, puffy sunflower made from two brown centres and six pointed yellow petals. The petal round joins both centres as you go, so there's nothing to sew. Use it as a bag charm, a brooch or a little gift.
materialsTable: Cotton DK in brown (centre) and yellow (petals). A few grams of each, so leftovers are perfect.
A small pinch of cotton or toy stuffing
Keyring or brooch pin for the back
materials: Cotton DK yarn in brown and yellow, a few grams of each
A little cotton or toy stuffing
notes: The centres are worked in a continuous spiral. Don't join the rounds. A stitch marker in the first stitch helps you count.
You make two centres. The yellow petal round goes through both of them at once, and that is what joins them.
tr here is the US treble crochet (UK double treble): yarn over twice before you insert the hook.
Crochet a little tightly so the stuffing doesn't show and the petals stand up.

sections.title: Part 1: Centre
sections.note: Make 2 the same. Work in a continuous spiral, don't join the rounds.

rounds.text: sl st in the next st and fasten off. Tuck the tail to the back. Make a second centre the same way.

sections.title: Part 2: Petals
sections.note: The petals are worked through both centres at the same time. You will make 6 petals.
intro: **Join:** Hold the two centres together, back sides facing each other and the stitches lined up. Insert your hook through one stitch of both centres and attach yellow with a sl st.
steps: ch 1, sl st into the top of the tr (petal tip)
sl st in the next st
after: Make 5 petals this way. Each petal uses 2 stitches of the centre (12 sts = 6 petals).
**Stuff:** Before the last petal, push a little cotton between the two centres through the open gap. Don't overfill.
**Last petal:** Make the 6th petal the same way and end with a sl st into the first sl st. Fasten off and weave in the ends.
sections.short: Short version: ch 2, dc, tr, ch 1, sl st in tip, tr, dc (all in one st), ch 2, sl st in next st.

finishing: Weave in any ends you can still see, hiding them between the two centres.
Optional: thread a jump ring through the tip of one petal and add a keyring, or sew a brooch pin to the back.
chartNote: One centre from the middle out, then the petal round.
variations: Use white petals and a yellow centre for a daisy, or pink petals for a cosmos. For a bigger flower, add Rnd 3 to both centres, (sc, inc) x6 for 18 sts, and make 9 petals.

tracker.text: Centre 1 (brown), Rnd 1: 6 sc in a magic ring
Centre 1, Rnd 2: inc in each st around. sl st, fasten off.
Centre 2 (brown), Rnd 1: 6 sc in a magic ring
Centre 2, Rnd 2: inc in each st around. sl st, fasten off.
Hold both centres together, back sides facing. Join yellow with a sl st through both.
Petals 1–5: ch 2, dc in next st, tr in same st, ch 1, sl st in tip, tr, dc in same st, ch 2, sl st in next st
Stuff the centre lightly through the gap.
Petal 6, same as before, sl st in the first sl st. Fasten off and weave in ends.

faq.q: Do I need to sew anything?
faq.a: No. The yellow petal round goes through both brown centres at once, so it joins them while you make the petals.

faq.q: What is tr in this pattern?
faq.a: tr is the US treble crochet: yarn over twice, then pull through two loops three times. In UK terms it is called a double treble (dtr).
Yes. Add a third round to each centre, (sc, inc) x6 for 18 stitches, then make 9 petals instead of 6. You can also use thicker yarn and a bigger hook.
